what: PTC makes engineering software. Creo is used to design physical products in three dimensions, Windchill manages the data and revisions behind those designs, and Codebeamer manages the software inside modern products.
customers: Manufacturers of cars, machinery, aerospace, electronics and medical devices.
money: Windchill, Codebeamer and service lifecycle software
moat: Software holding the master record of how a product is designed and built, where migrating means converting decades of engineering data and retraining engineers.
risks: Manufacturing customers defer software spending in downturns
Analyst targets imply the shares are already fully valued
Debt of about $1.6 billion against little cash
Growth depends on moving customers to higher-priced subscriptions
opportunities: Revenue grew about 19% last year with an 84% gross margin
Operating margin of 36% with very high subscription renewal rates
Software-defined products need exactly the lifecycle management it sells
watch: Annual recurring revenue growth in constant currency.
